_readme: Sub-communities within, and adjacent to, the Saraswat fold. Boundaries between these groups are historically fluid and locally contested; the archive records what a family says about itself rather than adjudicating.

items.name: Goud Saraswat Brahmin
items.region: Goa, coastal Karnataka, Kerala, coastal Maharashtra
items.note: The largest Konkani-speaking Saraswat group. Divided by matha affiliation into Vaishnava (Kashi Math, Partagali) and Smarta (Kavale) families.

items.name: Chitrapur Saraswat
items.note: A distinct Saraswat community centred on the Shri Chitrapur Math at Shirali. Surnames are usually village names — Nadkarni, Hattangadi, Kaikini, Padukone.

items.name: Rajapur Saraswat Brahmin
items.note: Konkani-speaking Saraswats of the Rajapur region of the southern Maharashtra coast.

items.name: Kudaldeshkar Gaud Brahmin
items.note: A Gaud Brahmin community of the Kudal region, closely associated with the Saraswats.

items.name: Bardeskar / Pednekar Saraswat
items.note: Saraswat families identified by the Goan taluka of origin.

items.name: Kashmiri Saraswat
items.region: Kashmir valley and the Indian diaspora
items.note: The northern Saraswat branch, associated with the original Sarasvati river homeland.

items.name: Punjabi Saraswat
items.note: Saraswat Brahmins of the north-west, named for the Sarasvati river.

items.name: Daivadnya
items.note: A Konkani-speaking community, closely tied to the Saraswats socially and linguistically but distinct in origin and tradition. Included because families intermarry and share villages, kuladevatas and records.

items.name: Other / not recorded
items.note: Use where the sub-community is unknown or does not fit the categories above.
